en: Now in this API folder, this API web app
here,
I have the actual Bun backend for this
project, for this social network. And that's
of course the core focus of this section.
There we're also using Bun for package
management. So for installing the
dependencies of this project, though that's
mostly just one dependency, the
awesome BetterAuth library, which we use for
authentication so that I don't have to build
all the authentication logic myself.
But other than that, there are no external
dependencies in there. Most importantly,
there is no other framework or anything in
there because Bun can really handle it all
on its own.
Because what we're building here is a REST
API in the end, and you find all the code
for that in the source folder. In that
source folder, we got an index.ts file
and we got a server.ts file, and these 2 are
our root entry points, so to say, because
index.ts indeed is the file that gets
when we start the dev server or the
production server with these commands as you
see.
And in index.ts, I am importing from the
server file
and I in the end create my web server.
Other than that, I also run my database
migrations here in case you didn't do that
yet. There is a separate script for that.
We had this db migrate script there and I'll
get back to the database migrations. But in
that index.ts file, I also invoke them again
to make sure that the database is up to date
is set up properly and then I check this to
throw an error early if something goes wrong
with the database before we start the server
so that we only start the server if the
database is set up correctly.
And then in server.ts, we do the actual
interesting stuff. We use Bun serve in
createServer, which is that function we call
from index.ts. So we run Bun serve and
return the result to spin up a Bun-powered
server.
That is how you do create a server with Bun
using bun serve.
I configure my port in there. That is one of
the options I take here or the only option
actually and the default is set to 3000 here
but we could override this.
And then I register some routes
using this routes feature the Bun server
supports.
That's just a shortcut for that and these
are imported from our routes file and of
course we'll explore those too.
And then I'm also using the fetch method in
addition to the routes, which you can of
course do
to have my main routes, but then this here,
this fetch method as a fallback for all the
other requests that are not handled by
routes.
And I'm using that here for NotFound errors
because if we reach this point here, we know
that the user tried to
access a route that just doesn't exist
because the registered routes are handled
first. So if you make it here, we clearly
tried to visit a non-registered route and
that's why I return a NotFound error here.
And I also handle the special options
request and that's just there for the
browser to handle preflight requests,
CORS-related preflight requests. And
attached you find a resource where you can
learn more about CORS if that's brand new to
you.
Speaking of CORS, I also have a middleware
setup, so to say, a helper function
which I wrap around all my responses here as
you see, and that's coming from the HTTP
CORS file in my project. So this file here,
and in there I simply set up a function
where I take a response which I'm about to
send in the end,
I take it as an input and I augment it to
add certain headers, CORS headers, because
since this is a REST API that will be
accessed by a frontend single-page
application running on a different domain
potentially will be having CORS problems if
we don't add those headers on the REST API.
Again, attached is that resource with more
details about CORS if that's brand new to
you.
But that's just a little helper function
which makes sure that whenever I wrap it
around a response, it adds those headers.
You can think of it as a middleware kind of,
so to say.
And that's how the server is generally set
up. But of course, there is a lot to dive
deeper, and we'll do that therefore.
